canonical_title: AgentRewardBench: Evaluating Automatic Evaluations of Web Agent Trajectories
authors: Xing Han Lù; Amirhossein Kazemnejad; Nicholas Meade; Arkil Patel; Dongchan Shin; Alejandra Zambrano; Karolina Stańczak; Peter Shaw; Christopher J. Pal; Siva Reddy
research_object: benchmark construction and evaluation of automatic LLM judges for web-agent trajectories
evaluation_granularity: full trajectory with three binary dimensions
input_representation: trajectory observations including screenshots/DOM/accessibility tree plus reasoning and actions
output_signal: success; side effects; repetition labels and judge predictions
training_required: no for benchmark; no model training reported for evaluated prompted judges
benchmarks: AgentRewardBench: five source benchmarks; official 196 dev / 1106 test trajectories
policy_models: four source agent families; twelve evaluated LLM judges
reported_metrics: precision primary; recall and F1 auxiliary
reported_main_result: 1302 expert-reviewed trajectories and 3906 binary annotations; no evaluated judge was consistently best across all dimensions
notes: THIS_WORK reuses the dataset and official split but studies frozen lightweight structural evaluators rather than the paper's prompted LLM-judge comparison; shared data provenance precludes independent external-validation wording.

canonical_title: Web-Shepherd: Advancing PRMs for Reinforcing Web Agents
authors: Hyungjoo Chae; Seonghwan Kim; Junhee Cho; Seungone Kim; Seungjun Moon; Gyeom Hwangbo; Dongha Lim; Minjin Kim; Yeonjun Hwang; Minju Gwak; Dongwook Choi; Minseok Kang; Gwanhoon Im; ByeongUng Cho; Hyojun Kim; Jun Han; Taeyoon Kwon; Minju Kim; Beong-woo Kwak; Dongjin Kang; Jinyoung Yeo
research_object: trained process reward models for web-agent action quality and reward-guided search
input_representation: text or vision observation; action; task checklist
output_signal: continuous step reward from judgment-label probabilities
training_required: yes: LoRA training on WebPRM Collection
policy_models: Qwen2.5/Qwen3 text and vision reward models; web policies under guided search
reported_metrics: MRR; step accuracy; trajectory accuracy; task success rate
reported_main_result: Web-Shepherd 8B text reports 97.8 MRR and 85.0 trajectory accuracy on the WebArena portion of WebRewardBench; guided search raises WebArena-Lite success from 23.64 to 34.55

canonical_title: AgentRM: Enhancing Agent Generalization with Reward Modeling
authors: Yu Xia; Jingru Fan; Weize Chen; Siyu Yan; Xin Cong; Zhong Zhang; Yaxi Lu; Yankai Lin; Zhiyuan Liu; Maosong Sun
research_object: reward modeling for agent-policy generalization and test-time search
evaluation_granularity: trajectory candidate scoring during Best-of-N or beam search
input_representation: task trajectory and task context for heterogeneous agent environments
output_signal: scalar reward used to select generated trajectories
benchmarks: WebShop; Alfworld; Sciworld; BabyAI; Jericho; Pddl; Maze; ToolQuery; ToolOperation
policy_models: LLM agents with Best-of-N and beam-search selection
reported_metrics: success rate; progress rate; average reward
reported_main_result: The explicit reward model with Best-of-5 reports an average score of 61.5 versus 52.7 for greedy decoding across the nine evaluated tasks
notes: Reward model supports policy search across mixed agent tasks; it is not a frozen benchmark-level trajectory classifier with the same targets or split.

research_object: benchmarking trajectory outcome and step process reward models for computer-use agents
evaluation_granularity: trajectory-level outcome reward and key-step process reward
input_representation: RGB screenshots plus reasoning/actions from computer-use trajectories
training_required: no for benchmark; yes for proposed reward-model training

canonical_title: WebGraphEval: Multi-Turn Trajectory Evaluation for Web Agents using Graph Representation
authors: Yaoyao Qian; Yuanli Wang; Jinda Zhang; Yun Zong; Meixu Chen; Hanhan Zhou; Jindan Huang; Yifan Zeng; Xinyu Hu; Chan Hee Song; Danqing Zhang
venue_or_status: NeurIPS 2025 Workshop: Multi-Turn Interactions in Large Language Models
research_object: graph-structured evaluation of multiple web-agent trajectories
evaluation_granularity: cross-multi-trajectory action graph with trajectory-level and agent-level aggregation
input_representation: canonicalized textual actions and URLs merged into a weighted directed action graph; LLM-derived success and necessity labels
output_signal: success and failure association; necessity; redundancy; path optimality; step inflation; graph complexity; critical/trap/bottleneck edges; cross-agent strategy profiles
training_required: no evaluator training; LLM inference is used for action canonicalization, success judging, and necessity annotation
uses_rule_based_eval: yes: deterministic graph construction and structural statistics after LLM annotation
benchmarks: WebArena; 812 tasks; 4768 trajectories from six agent frameworks
policy_models: Jace.AI; IBM CUGA; Learn by Interact; UI-TARS; OpenAI CUA; BrowserUse
reported_metrics: success rate; average steps; necessity rate; graph complexity; step inflation; reward-propagated node values; success-weighted edge categories
reported_main_result: The official paper analyzes 4768 WebArena trajectories and reports structural efficiency, redundancy, and critical decision patterns across six agents.
code_available: project/demo linked by official arXiv record; no repository verified
data_available: trajectory corpus described in paper; no separate dataset release verified
notes: Does WebGraphEval study structural trajectory evaluation? YES. It is the closest structural evaluation analogue, but it aggregates many trajectories into task graphs, uses different WebArena runs and no equivalent split, relies on LLM annotations, reports graph/efficiency analyses rather than per-trajectory expert-label prediction, and has no equivalent blind-heldout protocol.

canonical_title: Where Did It Go Wrong? Process-Level Evaluation of Web Agents with Semantic State Tracking
authors: Jiwan Chung; JiHyuk Byun; Vibhav Vineet; Seon Joo Kim
research_object: process-level evaluation and failure diagnosis of web agents through environment-level semantic state tracking
evaluation_granularity: trajectory summaries plus step/skill diagnostics and cross-trajectory bifurcation localization
input_representation: deterministic semantic MDP state/action traces recorded behind the GUI
output_signal: terminal success; exploration success; execution success; information coverage; skill invocation; GUI/semantic step efficiency; wrong-branch, delayed-commit, and premature-commit diagnostics
training_required: no evaluator training; metrics and failure localization are derived deterministically from the semantic MDP trace
uses_llm_or_vlm: yes: evaluated agents include VLMs and API systems, but the evaluator itself is not model-based
uses_rule_based_eval: yes: semantic verifier and MDP-derived metrics
benchmarks: WebStep; 1800 task instances across 10 deterministic self-hosted websites
policy_models: Fara-7B; GUI-Owl-1.5-8B; UI-TARS-1.5-7B; Qwen3.5-122B; OpenAI CUA; Claude CUA
reported_metrics: terminal, exploration, and execution success rates; information coverage; GUI and semantic steps; skill invocation; bifurcation distributions
reported_main_result: Process metrics separate agents with similar terminal success and localize distinct skill and trajectory failure modes.
code_available: project page available; code announced as coming soon
notes: Does WebStep evaluate the same target/protocol as THIS_WORK? NO. It diagnoses semantic-state exploration, execution, skills, and bifurcations in a purpose-built deterministic environment; THIS_WORK predicts frozen expert outcome dimensions from lightweight trajectory morphology under the AgentRewardBench blind-heldout protocol.
